Hot temperatures and lower than usual rainfall are forecast for the country from October to December.
This comes amid forecasts of extreme heat next year.
A strong El Niño event has formed in the Pacific Ocean and is likely to become a very strong event this spring, according to the South African Weather Service (Saws).
“The latest weekly average sea surface temperature anomalies over the eastern central tropical Pacific Ocean are already exceeding the threshold that defines a very strong El Niño.
“The latest predictions are indicative that the El Niño will likely intensify further to become the strongest event in living memory.”
A strong El Niño refers to an event where three-monthly average sea surface temperature anomalies over the eastern central tropical Pacific Ocean are exceeding 1.5°C with respect to climatology, while during a very strong El Niño this part of the ocean is 2°C warmer than normal. The latest forecasts indicate the current event is likely to exceed the 3°C threshold.
The latest seasonal forecast by Saws for October to December indicates below-normal rainfall is the most likely outcome over most of South Africa. This period is also very likely to be associated with above-normal temperatures.
Similar conditions are expected into January.
“The expected very strong El Niño of 2026/27, in combination with global warming, will likely result in 2027 being the warmest year ever recorded.
”The 2015/16 very strong El Niño event brought unprecedented heatwaves to the Southern African region. In the 11 years that have since passed, the Southern African region has also continued to warm. If the 2026/27 El Niño event brings the expected below-normal rainfall to Southern Africa, it is likely a high frequency of heatwaves will co-occur. These heatwaves have the potential to be severe."
Updated forecasts will be shared in coming months as the Saws said it will closely monitor the extent of expected heatwaves and water scarcity.

New Delhi: Homegrown Unified Payments Interface (UPI) processed a record 24.51 billion transactions worth Rs 29.8 lakh crore in August, primarily fuelled by Raksha Bandhan, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
The UPI transactions in value terms were Rs 29.8 lakh crore, near a record high of Rs 29.9 lakh crore in May and July 2026.
As per the data released on Tuesday, UPI transactions in volume terms touched a record of 24.51 billion in August, much higher than 23.66 billion in the previous month. The volume was 22.72 billion in June and 23.2 billion in May of this year.
The value of transactions was Rs 29.82 lakh crore in August, up from Rs 24.85 lakh crore in the same month a year ago, registering 20% annual growth.
At the same time, UPI volume rose by 22% on an annual basis to 24.51 billion in August as against 19.63 billion in the same month last year, according to NPCI data.
National Payments Corporation of India, an initiative of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Indian Banks’ Association, is an umbrella organisation for operating retail payments and settlement systems in India (IBA).
It runs the UPI used for real-time payments between peers or at merchants’ end while making purchases.
The volume growth in August was further bolstered by festive activity such as Raksha Bandhan, which naturally drove a surge in everyday peer-to-peer (P2P) transfers and small-ticket gifting, and consistent aggregate transaction value with an increase in volume over the past three months underscores the expanding reach and depth of the UPI ecosystem, Cashfree Payments co-founder Reeju Datta said. Looking ahead, he said, the upcoming festive season presents an exciting growth frontier.
As the festive season approaches and new use cases such as credit on UPI start to mature, continued investment in resilient, intelligent infrastructure will be key to sustaining India’s leadership in digital payments, Network People Services Technologies (NPST) co-founder and CEO Deepak Chand Thakur said.
As far as overseas presence is concerned, UPI now is accepted in 11 countries, with Uzbekistan being the latest entry. The other countries where UPI is accepted are Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Bhutan, Qatar, Sri Lanka, Cambodia, and Greece.
The UPI, launched on August 25, 2016, has transformed India’s digital payments landscape, with transaction value surging from Rs 0.07 lakh crore in FY17 to around Rs 314 lakh crore in FY26, a more than 4,000-fold increase over the decade. Annual UPI transaction volume rose from 1.78 crore in 2016-17 to more than 24,162 crore in 2025-26, an almost 13,000-fold increase.

The weather department has warned of thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and intense to very intense spells of rain at isolated places across the state. Light to moderate rainfall is likely to continue at several places in Uttarakhand until September 7.

In Rudraprayag district, heavy and continuous rainfall continues to lash several areas, while dense fog has enveloped the hilly regions, significantly reducing visibility. The combination of rain and fog has disrupted travel in the district, causing difficulties for local residents. The adverse weather has also affected normal life in rural areas, where persistent rainfall and excessive soil moisture have brought agricultural activities to a halt.
According to the IMD forecast, heavy rain is likely at isolated places in several districts on Thursday, including Dehradun, Tehri, Uttarkashi, Nainital, Champawat, Udham Singh Nagar, Pithoragarh and Bageshwar. Thunderstorms with lightning and intense to very intense spells of rain are likely across all districts.
On September 4, heavy rain is likely at isolated places in Nainital, Champawat, Dehradun, Haridwar and Bageshwar, while thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and intense to very intense spells of rain are expected across the state. On September 5, heavy rain is likely at isolated places in Dehradun, Haridwar and Pauri districts, with thunderstorms and lightning likely at isolated places in all districts of the state.
On Tuesday, the Uttarakhand State Disaster Management Authority (USDMA) issued a red alert for heavy to extremely heavy rainfall across parts of the state till 10 am on September 2. According to the alert, very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall, accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and intense spells of rain, was likely for the next 18 hours from 3:58 pm that day, the disaster management authority said.
Areas likely to be affected include Chaukhutiya, Bhikiyasen, Ranikhet, Bhanoli, Katarmal, Jainti, Ramnagar, Bhimtal, Haldwani, Mukteshwar, Kotabagh, Bhawali and Dwarahat, along with adjoining areas.
Comes amid heightened alert across the Himalayan region
The warnings for Uttarakhand come at a time when the wider Himalayan belt remains on edge following catastrophic flash floods in neighbouring Nepal. Flash floods triggered along the Trishuli River near the China-Nepal border in late August have left over 1,000 people dead in Nepal, according to that country's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA), with thousands more injured or still missing, including a large number of foreign nationals.

Nepali authorities have also flagged continued risk of fresh flash floods in northern districts such as Nuwakot and Rasuwa, underscoring how unstable conditions across the central Himalayas remain heading into September.
While the Uttarakhand alerts are a separate weather system, the proximity and timing add to concerns among disaster management authorities in India's hill states, where saturated soil, swollen rivers and fragile mountain terrain increase the risk of landslides and flash flooding during sustained spells of heavy rain.

Extreme Heat Expected On First Full Weekend Of College Football
Marshall Shepherd, Senior Contributor
Updated
4 min read

As the first full weekend of college football approaches, extreme heat will be a feature for many locations east of the Rocky Mountains. The National Weather Service is forecasting above-normal temperatures in many places for the first weekend of September. The culprit is a persistent area of high pressure or what many outlets refer to a heat dome these days.
"A dangerous late-summer heat wave will continue to bring extremely hot temperatures to the central U.S. through the weekend into next week as a large mid/upper ridge remains centered over the region," wrote NOAA's Weather Prediction Center forecasters. "High temperatures well into the 90s and low 100s combined with high humidity and very warm overnight lows in the mid 70s will result in widespread areas of Major to Extreme Heat Risk and a concern for heat-related illnesses," they went on to say. Similar hot conditions are expected in the Southeast and southern part of the Mid-Atlantic region. There is a hint of relief Sunday as a cold front slides through the region.
Some of the best college football in the country happens in the SEC, Big 10, and ACC conferences. Many of those schools are expecting high temperatures in the upper nineties as shown in the map above. Many places could see temperatures at or above 100 degrees Fahrenheit. When you factor in the humidity, the heat index and Wet-Bulb Globe Temperatures move into dangerous territory. As context, typical high temperatures on September 5 in Norman, Oklahoma are usually in the mid-to-upper eighties. They could get close to 100 degrees F on Saturday.
NWS statistics continue to show that heat is the deadliest weather event annually in the U.S. over the past thirty years. This presents challenges for schools, fans, and workers. In "week zero" of the college football season, we saw a preview of the extreme heat - college football convergence. The University of Southern California played San Jose State University under sweltering heat conditions last Saturday. Many fans chose to stay home or had to leave the stadium. According to ESPN, some fans passed out or experienced other heat-related illnesses.

Candidly, this is not your grandfather's Septembersof the past. Yes, I know it is hot on Labor Day Weekend in many parts of the country, but it is not supposed to be 10 degress or more above average temperatures. September 1 is the beginning of meteorological fall, and over the past several decades, temperatures are continuing to increase. Yet, college football season and pre-game training leading up to it start in some of the hottest conditions of the year. While many football programs are providing measures to mitigate the impact of heat Saturday on players, officials, fans, and workers, a bigger question looms in decades to come about the timing of the sport.
If attending games on Saturday, I urge people to be extra cognizant of their physical well-being, available resources, and best practices. Here are my recommendations:
Limit alcohol consumption.
Stay hydrated with water.
Seek cooling stations and other resources being offered at the stadium.
Monitor how you are feeling. Signs of heat exhaustion include Heat exhaustion can develop quickly, but is often treatable when addressed early.
Be aware of symptoms of heat exhaustion including nausea, dizziness, excessive sweating, fatigue, clammy skin. Heat stroke is more serious and requires medical attention immediately.
Wear light-colored and loose-fitting clothing.
Apply sunscreen.
Know where medical attendants and services are located and how to contact them in an emergency.
